Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

rorabaughapril@gmail.com

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor with an Ed.D. in Community Care and Counseling: Traumatology and more than 15 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, and program leadership, I bring a strong commitment to providing high-quality, trauma-informed care to adolescents and families.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with youth experiencing complex behavioral health challenges, trauma histories, family instability, and barriers to accessing appropriate treatment. In my leadership role with Partners Health Management, I have overseen behavioral health initiatives across a 15-county service area, supervised multidisciplinary teams, and helped develop and implement specialized programs designed to improve access to services, strengthen care coordination, and reduce unnecessary higher levels of care.  One of my greatest professional strengths is combining clinical expertise with operational leadership. I have experience supporting clinical decision-making, establishing effective workflows, monitoring quality and compliance, mentoring staff, and collaborating with families, community providers, hospitals, and child welfare agencies. I understand the importance of developing a clinical environment where staff feel supported, families feel heard, and adolescents receive individualized, evidence-based treatment.

My doctoral research focused on the experiences of social workers placing youth in residential treatment within North Carolina's child welfare system. This work further strengthened my understanding of the challenges adolescents and families face when appropriate community-based behavioral health services are unavailable. I am particularly passionate about developing programs that intervene earlier, promote stability, and help youth receive effective treatment in the least restrictive appropriate setting.

The opportunity to contribute to the development and leadership of Adolescent Wellness Academy's North Carolina program is especially appealing. I would welcome the opportunity to help establish a strong clinical culture, support staff development, build community partnerships, and ensure that adolescents and families receive compassionate, effective, and accountable care.  Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to adolescent mental health could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's success.

Sincerely,
April L. Rorabaugh, Ed.D., LCMHC

Sincerely,

Because I was passionate about my work and continually identifying new opportunities for growth, I often found myself moving from one project or initiative to the next without taking sufficient time to pause, appreciate what I had accomplished, or recharge. While this drive contributed to the growth and success of the practice, it also taught me the importance of sustainability, boundaries, and intentional self-care.  This experience has helped me recognize that effective leadership is not simply about how much you can accomplish, but also about creating a sustainable pace that supports long-term effectiveness, sound decision-making, and personal well-being. I have learned the value of being more intentional about prioritizing, setting boundaries, and making space to reflect on accomplishments rather than constantly focusing on the next goal. I view this continued growth as an important part of becoming a more balanced and effective leader.

October 23, 2026 

Dear Hiring Committee, 

Thank you for taking the time to review my resume and cover letter. I am writing to express my enthusiasm for the opportunity to continue my experience working as a Registered Mental Health Counseling Intern at  Adolescent Wellness Academy. I received a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and am a recent graduate with my Masters in Mental Health Counseling from the University of Miami. 

As a motivated and compassionate clinician, I am interested in expanding my experience of working with evidence-based treatment modalities. 

My educational experiences have helped me to build my knowledge and experience for working as a registered mental health counseling intern. I have a strong academic background in psychology, as well as a strong interest in working with children and their families to address mental health challenges at an early age, including Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Anxiety, and Depression. Through my recent experiences working as a practicum intern at Nicklaus Children’s Hospital and the Institute for Individual and Family Counseling, I was able to establish a strong foundation in conceptualizing cases, applying interventions and building rapport. 

In my previous experience working at Florida International University’s Summer Treatment Program, I had the opportunity to work directly with children and their families, providing support in areas such as emotional regulation, coping skills, and behavioral management. These experiences have provided a good foundation in implementing therapeutic strategies tailored to the unique needs of young children, as well as solidified my interest in child and adolescent mental health. 

I have a passion for working with programs that help to provide low-cost services for a diverse population, as highlighted in my experience working as a practicum intern at the institute for Individual and Family Counseling. I believe that my strong communication skills and dedication will allow for a wonderful learning experience as I continue my work in the field of mental health counseling.  

I have included my resume and look forward to the possibility of discussing further my qualifications. Please feel welcome to contact me at your earliest convenience. I look forward to hearing from you. 

Respectfully, 
Morgan Reilly

Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Rebecca Ubertini

Hiring Committee

Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

I understand the importance of accuracy, organization, confidentiality, and clear communication when handling sensitive patient information and coordinating appointments.

In addition to my medical background, my ten-plus years in animal behavioral science have provided me with extensive experience working with families to understand their needs, develop individualized plans of care, and support them in implementing those plans. This experience has strengthened my ability to build relationships, communicate effectively, provide guidance, and approach each situation with patience, empathy, and attention to detail.

My remote work experience has also taught me how to work independently, manage competing priorities, stay organized, and maintain productivity while collaborating with a team. I understand that effective patient care coordination requires compassion, reliability, and the ability to ensure patients and families feel informed and supported throughout their care journey.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my diverse experience, strong organizational skills, and commitment to helping others to your team. I am confident that my background would allow me to make a positive contribution to your organization while helping patients and families navigate their care with confidence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills align with the needs of your team.

**Sincerely,**

Sam

candidates.cover_letter:
My academic background in psychology and my professional experience supporting individuals and families have shaped my commitment to helping people access the resources and support they need to thrive. I was particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s philosophy of treating people, not symptoms, and its commitment to creating a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental environment where adolescents and their families can heal and grow together. I believe that helping someone access care begins with making them feel heard, respected, and supported. I would be excited to contribute to this mission as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator by helping adolescents and families navigate the admissions process with compassion, clarity, and understanding.

I earned my Bachelor of Arts from Widener University, where I studied Psychology and Gender and Women’s Studies and minored in International Relations. My academic background provided me with a foundation in human behavior, interpersonal relationships, and the importance of understanding individuals within their broader social and family contexts. Through my academic and professional experiences, I have developed an appreciation for person-centered approaches that recognize each individual's unique circumstances, strengths, and challenges. I would bring this perspective to interactions with families who may be navigating uncertainty or seeking mental health support for their adolescents.

In my current role as an Employment Specialist at DiscoverAbility, I work directly with individuals to identify opportunities that align with their goals, strengths, and needs. I guide participants through the employment process by assisting with applications, developing resumes and cover letters, identifying appropriate opportunities, and maintaining accurate documentation of their progress. This role has strengthened my ability to build rapport, communicate information clearly, provide individualized guidance, and manage responsibilities with attention to detail. Previously, as an intern with Elwyn’s Early Learning Services, I gained experience supporting young children with developmental delays and disabilities and their families. I contributed to efforts focused on promoting child development, strengthening family capacity, and helping families access the support they needed. These experiences reinforced the importance of patience, empathy, and collaboration when working with individuals and families navigating unfamiliar or challenging circumstances.

My experience with Maryland Hunger Solutions further strengthened my ability to connect individuals with essential resources. Through outreach and advocacy initiatives, I collaborated with community partners and assisted individuals in accessing programs such as SNAP, local food banks, and school meal services. I also helped develop communication materials, including Spanish-language resources, to improve accessibility for Spanish-speaking communities. This experience taught me that connecting people with services requires more than providing information; it requires listening to their concerns, explaining available resources in accessible language, and helping them understand their next steps. As someone fluent in both English and Spanish, I would bring this same commitment to culturally responsive communication when interacting with adolescents, parents, and referral partners.

What stands out to me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is its recognition that supporting adolescents also means supporting their families. Seeking mental health treatment can be an overwhelming process for parents and teens alike, and the first interaction with an admissions team can help establish a sense of trust and reassurance. I would approach these conversations with compassion, professionalism, and respect, recognizing the importance of helping each family feel heard while guiding them toward appropriate next steps. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my communication, organizational, and client-support skills to an admissions process that reflects AWA’s commitment to individualized care, family involvement, and lasting growth.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background in psychology, experience supporting individuals and families, and commitment to accessible, person-centered services could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s mission.

I am writing to express my interest in a teaching position within your school district, specifically in Media Arts, Broadcasting, English, or related subject areas. Sincerely,

When a parent reaches out to the Adolescent Wellness Center, they are often calling on one of the most stressful days of their life. They need an intake voice who balances clinical precision with immense empathy. As an experienced admissions supervisor and intake professional returning to behavioral health, I am writing to express my enthusiastic interest in the Remote Intake Coordinator position. After taking a planned two-year break to focus full-time on my family as a stay-at-home mom, I am eager to re-enter the workforce in a role dedicated to meaningful, life-changing work for youth and their support systems.

My background directly eliminates any technical or operational ramp-up time for your team. Across my career in treatment management, I progressed from an Admissions Coordinator to Admissions Supervisor. I am deeply proficient in industry-standard software, including KIPU and Salesforce. I’m also experience at independently verifying complex insurance eligibility and navigating prior authorizations smoothly from a remote environment.

Beyond clinical administration, my recent background includes high-volume guest relations within the Atlantic City casino and hospitality industry. Although my previous positions have primarily been in person, I have experience independently managing work-related responsibilities outside of my regular work environment. I am organized, dependable, adaptable, and confident in my ability to learn new systems and succeed in a remote position.

I would appreciate the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and genuine passion for mental health to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of joining your team.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and relationship-building skills to your admissions team. I am confident that my background and commitment to exceptional service would allow me to make an immediate and meaningful contribution to your organization.

Sincerely,
Sharmen N. Clark

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for a position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. When I learned about your work supporting adolescents and their families through mental health treatment, I immediately felt that this was an organization where my education, professional experience, and personal passion for helping others could come together in a meaningful way.

I hold a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from Southern New Hampshire University, graduating with a 3.79 GPA, and I am currently pursuing my master's degree at Grand Canyon University. Continuing my education in this field reflects how seriously I take my goal of building a career centered around mental health and helping others.

My professional background includes more than ten years of experience in behavioral health, customer service, administrative support, and leadership. Earlier in my career, I worked as a Mental Health Technician at Cypress Psychiatric Hospital, where I provided direct support to patients in an inpatient psychiatric setting. I monitored behavior, documented observations for clinical teams, assisted with crisis prevention and de-escalation, and supported patients with daily living and therapeutic activities.

That experience gave me an appreciation for how important it is to have people around you who are willing to listen without judgment and remain calm when someone is struggling. I learned that sometimes the way you communicate with someone can make a difficult situation feel a little less overwhelming. Those are lessons I have carried with me throughout my career.

My more recent experience as a Customer Service Representative and Administrative Assistant has strengthened the organizational and communication skills I would bring to AWA. I have managed high volumes of calls, addressed concerns with empathy and professionalism, coordinated schedules and tasks, maintained accurate documentation, prepared reports, and handled sensitive information while maintaining confidentiality. I am comfortable learning new technology and regularly working with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams.

I am particularly interested in working with adolescents because I believe early support can make a lasting difference. Teenagers are navigating an incredibly important period of development, and having someone take their concerns seriously can matter more than people sometimes realize. I would approach each interaction with patience, respect, and the understanding that every adolescent and family has a different story and different needs.

I also understand that behavioral health is not only about supporting the individual receiving care. Families often need reassurance, clear communication, organization, and someone who can help them navigate what can be an unfamiliar and stressful process. My combination of behavioral health experience, psychology education, graduate-level study, and administrative and customer-service skills would allow me to support both the human and practical sides of that process.

I would be honored to bring my experience, compassion, reliability, and genuine interest in mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am eager to continue growing within the behavioral health field while pursuing my master's degree, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team dedicated to helping adolescents and families build healthier futures.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to speak with you about how my background and education could contribute to the work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Heather Morris

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With approximately 10 years of experience in the mental health and substance use treatment field, I have developed a strong understanding of the challenges individuals and families face when seeking behavioral health services. I am passionate about helping people access the care they need, and I believe my professional background, personal experiences, and commitment to compassionate, person-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Throughout my career, I have worked with individuals experiencing mental health challenges, substance use disorders, and co-occurring conditions. My experience in behavioral health has strengthened my communication, documentation, coordination, and client advocacy skills. I understand the importance of helping individuals navigate treatment options, communicating clearly with families and providers, and ensuring that people feel supported rather than overwhelmed when taking the first steps toward recovery. I also recognize that timely follow-up, accurate documentation, confidentiality, and organization are essential to helping individuals successfully access appropriate treatment.

In addition to my professional experience, I bring a personal understanding of the impact addiction and mental health challenges can have on individuals and families. I grew up in the foster care system with two parents who struggled with addiction. Those experiences gave me firsthand insight into the instability, uncertainty, and emotional challenges that children and families can experience when substance use affects a household. While my professional experience has provided me with the knowledge and skills to work in behavioral health, my personal experiences have shaped the compassion, empathy, and understanding I bring to every interaction. I recognize that behind every phone call is a person or family who may be experiencing fear, uncertainty, or desperation, and I believe those individuals deserve to be met with dignity, patience, and understanding.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it allows me to combine my behavioral health experience with my passion for helping individuals and families access appropriate treatment. Whether assisting a parent seeking care for their teenager or helping an adult explore treatment for substance use and co-occurring mental health concerns, I understand how important that first connection can be. As a U.S. Army veteran with a disciplined, dependable, and team-oriented approach, I am comfortable managing competing priorities, maintaining accurate documentation, and communicating effectively with patients, families, and multidisciplinary teams. Javen Owens

Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Most recently I worked overnight in a substance use treatment program, and for years before that I was a paramedic, so I have spent my career being the steady voice for people on some of their hardest days. I would be honored to bring that to families and clients making their first call for help.
As an Overnight Clinical Technician at CASA Trinity, I supported clients in recovery as a 1:1 mentor and documented their progress in the agency's EHR in compliance with NYS OASAS and 42 CFR confidentiality requirements. I coordinated with outside providers and referral sources, handled screening and transportation logistics, and joined weekly interdisciplinary case meetings. That work gave me hands-on experience with the intake-to-treatment pathway your coordinators guide families through, and with protecting the privacy of people seeking care.
My eight years as a paramedic and EMT Crew Chief taught me to build rapport quickly with frightened patients and families, explain what is happening in plain language, and give clear handoffs to physicians and nurses. Today, as a NYS Long Term Care Ombudsman, I investigate complaints, mediate among residents, families, and staff, and track every case through to resolution in organized records. I have also volunteered for years as a crisis advocate and as a moderator in mental health support communities, where I de-escalate people in distress and connect them with appropriate resources.
I know this role demands consistent follow-up and the discipline to manage your own pipeline. My current work is self-directed: I carry my own caseload, set my own priorities, and follow each case until it is resolved. I am comfortable with CRM and EHR documentation and learn new systems quickly, and I am eager to build further skills in Kipu and insurance verification.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a current Master of Social Work student at the University at Albany with a bachelor's degree in Human Development, a concentration in Special Education and Literacy, and a minor in Sociology, I bring a strong foundation in behavioral health, client advocacy, healthcare administration, and compassionate communication. I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it combines my professional experience with my passion for helping individuals and families access meaningful mental health support.

Throughout my professional experience as a Behavior Technician, I have worked directly with children and families navigating developmental, behavioral, and emotional challenges. These experiences strengthened my ability to establish trust, communicate sensitive information, maintain confidentiality, and provide individualized support. I understand that individuals seeking behavioral health services may be experiencing overwhelming circumstances, and I recognize the importance of approaching every interaction with patience, empathy, professionalism, and reassurance.

Additionally, my background in healthcare administration, including experience with electronic medical records such as Epic, has equipped me with valuable skills in documentation, organization, patient communication, and managing confidential information. My experience in administrative and client-facing positions has strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, respond to inquiries, maintain accurate records, and ensure individuals receive timely assistance.

As a graduate social work student, I am continuing to develop my knowledge of mental health, substance use, assessment, and person-centered approaches to care. My field experience supporting adolescents through educational and community-based programming has further reinforced my commitment to early intervention, advocacy, and connecting individuals with appropriate resources. I believe that access to quality care begins with the first interaction, and I would take pride in ensuring that every individual and family contacting your programs feels heard, respected, and supported.

I am confident that my combination of behavioral health experience, administrative skills, technological proficiency, and commitment to client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your organization's mission while continuing to grow professionally within the behavioral health field.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and dedication align with the needs of your team.

Sincerely,  
Catherine Frempong

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in behavioral health, human services, crisis intervention, and customer service, I am passionate about helping individuals and families navigate challenging situations and connect with the support they need. I would welcome the opportunity to use my communication skills, compassion, and attention to detail to help clients take the first step toward recovery and wellness.

In my previous roles as a Behavioral Health Technician at Gibault Children's Services and a Mental Health Technician at Harsha Behavioral Center, I provided direct support to individuals with behavioral and mental health needs, including children with autism and behavioral challenges. These experiences strengthened my ability to remain calm in difficult situations, listen attentively, respond appropriately to sensitive concerns, and communicate with individuals who may be experiencing emotional distress. I understand the importance of treating every individual with dignity, patience, and compassion, especially when they and their families are seeking help during vulnerable moments.

My experience as a Customer Care Representative with Continuum Global Solutions also prepared me to succeed in a client-facing admissions role. I handled incoming calls from healthcare professionals, answered questions, explained insurance policy information, and worked to resolve concerns efficiently. Combined with my behavioral health experience, this background has equipped me to communicate clearly, provide supportive service, and help people understand their options. I also bring experience with clinical documentation, HIPAA compliance, confidential information, and accurate recordkeeping, all of which are essential when managing admissions inquiries and coordinating care.

Additionally, my current experience in quality assurance has strengthened my ability to follow established procedures, review records for accuracy, identify discrepancies, and maintain compliance with organizational standards. I am organized, adaptable, dependable, and comfortable prioritizing responsibilities in fast-paced environments. I would bring these strengths to managing inquiries, documenting interactions, following up with prospective clients and families, and helping ensure a smooth transition from the initial call to the next step in the admissions process.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it combines my experience in behavioral health with my commitment to helping people access meaningful care. I would be proud to contribute to a team that recognizes the importance of making every caller feel heard, respected, and supported. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and dedication to compassionate service could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Kandyse Lewis

RE: Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager: I am writing to express my interest in the position of Virtual Admissions Coordinator for Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment. I am currently pursuing a Master of Arts in Counseling and Human Services with a concentration in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and I am eager to build upon my professional experience while developing my skills as a counselor in a clinical setting.

For nearly a decade, I have worked in secondary education with students and families from a wide range of backgrounds and circumstances. Throughout my career, I have had the opportunity to work alongside individuals from low-socioeconomic and historically disenfranchised populations, as well as individuals whose lives have been impacted by addiction, legal involvement, housing instability, and homelessness. These experiences have shaped the way I understand people and the circumstances that influence their lives. More importantly, they have reinforced my belief that every person deserves to be heard, treated with dignity, and supported without judgment.

My experience in education has taught me that meaningful change often begins with a trusting relationship. As an educator, I have learned to listen carefully, recognize when someone may be struggling beneath the surface, meet individuals where they are, and provide support while respecting their autonomy. I have also seen how trauma, substance use, socioeconomic barriers, family circumstances, and other challenges can affect a person's ability to succeed. These experiences have been an important part of my decision to pursue clinical mental health counseling and licensed addiction counseling.

As a graduate student, I am now seeking an opportunity to translate my academic preparation into meaningful clinical experience. I am most interested in strengthening my counseling skills alongside qualified professionals, developing greater confidence in clinical assessment and treatment, and becoming more intentional in how I support clients through difficult periods of their lives. At this present stage, curiosity, genuineness, and adaptability are the core values that drive my professional attitude. 
I would be grateful for the opportunity to learn and serve at the Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am eager to have the opportunity to grow within your organization while gaining the clinical experience necessary to become a compassionate, ethical, and effective practitioner.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my background, goals, and interest in potentially working with the Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Brianna L. Gabbard

Cover Letter – Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With experience in behavioral health, crisis support, and direct client services, I have developed a strong foundation in compassionate communication, active listening, and helping individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances. I am excited about the opportunity to bring these skills to an organization dedicated to supporting adolescents and their well-being.

My background includes working as a Registered Behavior Technician and providing intensive and respite services, where I support individuals with behavioral and developmental needs. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate effectively, remain patient under pressure, maintain professionalism, and approach each individual with empathy and respect. In addition, my work with DeafLEAD in a crisis-support role has reinforced the importance of building trust, responding thoughtfully to sensitive situations, and helping individuals feel heard during vulnerable moments.

I am currently working in a 100% remote position with DeafLEAD, which has provided me with direct experience managing professional responsibilities in a virtual work environment. I have a dedicated, private workspace equipped with the necessary technology, reliable high-speed internet, and the equipment needed to perform my duties effectively. I am confident in my ability to remain productive, communicate professionally, maintain confidentiality, and consistently complete my workload while working remotely. Transitioning into another fully virtual position would be a natural fit for my existing experience and established work environment.

I understand that the admissions process can be an important first step for families seeking behavioral health support for their children. I would approach this responsibility with compassion, organization, and attention to detail, ensuring that prospective families feel welcomed, informed, and supported as they explore available services. I am committed to creating positive first impressions, communicating clearly, and helping families navigate the admissions process with professionalism and sensitivity.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy by combining my behavioral health background, crisis-support experience, and established remote-work capabilities to support both families and the admissions team. I believe my commitment to helping others, adaptability, and ability to work independently would make me a valuable addition to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Serene Smith

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in behavioral healthcare, a background in pediatric mental health crisis intervention, and a Master’s degree in healthcare administration, I bring a combination of clinical knowledge, communication skills, and administrative understanding that aligns with the needs of this position. I am passionate about helping adolescents and their families navigate the process of accessing appropriate mental health and substance use treatment.

In my current role as a Mental Health Technician at SUN Behavioral Health in Erlanger, Kentucky, I work in a behavioral healthcare environment where patient safety, communication, confidentiality, and collaboration are essential. This experience has strengthened my understanding of behavioral health services and the importance of creating a supportive environment for individuals experiencing emotional and psychological challenges. I have developed the ability to remain professional in stressful situations, communicate effectively with members of an interdisciplinary team, and recognize the importance of treating every patient with dignity and respect.

Previously, I served as a Behavioral Health Specialist in the Emergency Department at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center, where I supported children and adolescents experiencing mental health crises. This experience gave me valuable insight into the challenges families face when seeking behavioral health services for their children. It also strengthened my understanding of the importance of timely access to care, clear communication, and collaboration among healthcare professionals. I recognize that connecting families with the appropriate level of treatment requires compassion, patience, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate sensitive information in a professional and supportive manner.

My Master’s degree in healthcare administration has further prepared me to contribute to the operational and coordination responsibilities of an admissions role. Through my education, I have developed a stronger understanding of healthcare systems, quality improvement, ethical decision-making, and the importance of efficient processes in supporting positive patient outcomes. I understand that an effective admissions process involves more than gathering information; it also requires helping families understand available services, coordinating next steps, maintaining accurate documentation, and communicating with appropriate team members to facilitate access to care.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines behavioral health, family engagement, and healthcare coordination. I would welcome the opportunity to help adolescents and their families navigate what can often be an overwhelming treatment-seeking process. I understand the importance of approaching these conversations without judgment, protecting confidential information, and helping families feel heard while ensuring their needs are communicated appropriately to the clinical team. I am also prepared to bring organization, accountability, and professionalism to a virtual work environment while maintaining a strong focus on responsiveness and service.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, educational background, and commitment to improving access to care could contribute to the admissions team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of helping adolescents and their families take meaningful steps toward treatment, recovery, and improved well-being.

Sincerely,
Stephenie Shelton

Monica Cockfield
Florence, SC
Msyc89@gmail.com

October 22, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy 

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With experience in behavioral health, admissions and intake coordination, therapeutic foster care, and crisis intervention, I believe my professional background and passion for helping others would make me a strong addition to your team.

Throughout my career, I have gained hands-on experience managing referrals, completing intake processes, coordinating placements, and communicating with families, providers, and community agencies. In my current roles as a Therapeutic Foster Care Case Manager and Overnight Emergency Placement Supervisor, I regularly assist individuals experiencing behavioral health challenges while ensuring they are connected with appropriate services and resources.

My experience working remotely has strengthened my ability to manage responsibilities independently, stay organized, maintain accurate documentation, and communicate effectively without constant supervision. I understand the importance of timely follow-up, confidentiality, and providing a positive experience from the initial point of contact through the coordination of services.

I also recognize that individuals and families seeking mental health or substance use treatment may be experiencing some of the most difficult moments of their lives. I pride myself on approaching every interaction with compassion, patience, and professionalism while helping individuals feel heard, supported, and informed about their next steps.

I hold a Bachelor's degree in Social Science with a minor in Psychology and a Master's degree in Criminal Justice. I am also currently pursuing my Master of Social Work degree at Troy University. My education and professional experience have provided me with a strong understanding of behavioral health needs, crisis intervention, and person-centered care.

I would appreciate the opportunity to bring my experience, strong work ethic, and commitment to helping others to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how I can contribute to the continued success of your programs.

Sincerely,
Monica Cockfield

candidates.cover_letter:
October 21, 2026

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinators
Dear Hiring Team,
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at AWA. Your mission to help not only the youth you serve, but the family as a whole is a strong match for the work I have done throughout my career.
For more than ten years, I have worked in roles where accuracy and confidentiality were not optional. As a Program Manager at Community Violence Solutions, I audited 100–200 client records every month in an Excel-based database, maintaining 100% accuracy and strict confidentiality. I managed high-volume documentation workflows against firm compliance deadlines, cross-checked data across multiple platforms, and produced reports for county, state, and federal funders. I also supervised a team of five to seven employees and trained them on data entry and documentation, so I know how to keep detail-oriented work consistent across a team. The work that I completed was all done with love and care for the family unit. We thrived in helping youth and families throughout their healing process. 
Earlier in my career, I managed active caseloads of 30 to 50+ clients at a time, completing intakes, case data entry, and monthly documentation for each one. I also provided customer and tech support in person and by chat as a part-time Customer Support Specialist at Sprint, handling setups, activations, and troubleshooting. Answering calls, working with limited supervision, and adjusting to changing priorities are things I do every day. I work comfortably in Word, Excel, Outlook, Google Workspace, Zoom, and Teams, and I have spent several years working fully remotely.
What I would bring to AWA most of all is a deep respect for the people behind the records. I have spent my career helping people in difficult moments, and I understand how important it is that sensitive information reaches only the right hands. I am eager to build on that foundation by learning HIPAA regulations and AWA,s procedures, and by developing into a dependable, high-quality member of your team. As a fully bilingual English and Spanish speaker, I also communicate clearly and professionally with a wide range of customers.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience can support your team, and I can be reached at 415-948-3875 or lray1214@gmail.com.

Sincerely,

Lucia Ray-Guillen

Inez D. Kearse
Covington, GA
470-301-4009 | inezdenice@gmail.com

October 21, 2026

Dear Hiring Team,

I believe the person answering that first phone call can make all the difference in whether someone takes the next step toward getting help. That is what caught my attention about this opportunity. You're not simply looking for someone to answer calls and schedule appointments. You're looking for someone who can recognize the importance of that moment, connect with the person on the other end of the phone, and help them move forward. That is exactly the kind of work I enjoy doing.

I bring a combination of remote admissions experience, behavioral health support, and genuine compassion for people who are navigating difficult circumstances. During my time with Ultimate Medical Academy, I worked remotely in admissions, interviewing prospective students, managing a high volume of inquiries, maintaining CRM records, and following up with individuals throughout the enrollment process. I ranked number one in my division and achieved 380% of my enrollment target. Those results came from more than meeting performance expectations. I understood how to build relationships, listen to people's needs, address their concerns, and remain consistent in my follow-through.

What makes my background especially relevant is that I also understand the importance of emotional support. Through my work with Youth Villages and my experience in family support counseling, I've worked with individuals and families facing behavioral challenges, emotional difficulties, and circumstances that require patience, compassion, and sound judgment. I've learned that people do not always know how to communicate what they need, especially when they're overwhelmed. Sometimes you have to listen beyond the initial question to understand how you can actually help.

I recognize that behavioral health admissions are different from educational admissions. Families seeking mental health or substance use treatment may be frightened, exhausted, or uncertain about what happens next. I would approach those conversations with the same care I would want someone to show my own family, while ensuring that inquiries, documentation, referrals, and follow-ups are handled professionally and accurately.

I'm comfortable working independently in a remote environment, managing multiple conversations and responsibilities, maintaining confidential information, and following through until the next step is clear. I would welcome the opportunity to learn your admissions processes and become a dependable part of the team supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

I am confident in what I bring to this position, but what matters most to me is the opportunity to use my experience in a way that genuinely impacts someone's life. I would love the opportunity to speak with you about how I can contribute to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Inez D. Kearse

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With nearly three years of experience in behavioral health, peer support, and community health services, I have developed strong communication, resource navigation, and care coordination skills that I believe would be valuable to your admissions team.

In my current role as a Community Health Worker and Peer Support Specialist at Healthcare Alternative Systems, I assist individuals experiencing mental health and substance use challenges by identifying their needs, connecting them with community resources, coordinating referrals, and providing follow-up support. Previously, as a Bilingual Community Support Specialist at Leyden Family Services and Mental Health Center: Living Room, I supported individuals experiencing emotional distress and behavioral health crises through active listening, de-escalation, safety assessments, and referrals to appropriate services.

Through my experience, I have gained familiarity with different behavioral health and supportive service programs, including intensive outpatient treatment, transitional living programs, specialized mental health rehabilitation facilities, and supportive housing. I understand the importance of considering an individual's needs and program eligibility when identifying appropriate resources. Although my experience has primarily focused on referrals and connecting individuals with services rather than formal treatment admissions, I am eager to expand my knowledge of PHP and IOP admissions, insurance verification, and intake coordination.

I am bilingual in English and Spanish, experienced in telephone outreach, and comfortable maintaining accurate and confidential documentation using CareLogic. As a Certified Recovery Support Specialist currently pursuing my Master of Social Work, I am committed to helping individuals and families access meaningful care.

What interests me most about this opportunity is the ability to support individuals from their very first interaction with a treatment program. I understand that reaching out for help can be overwhelming, and I would welcome the opportunity to provide compassionate guidance while helping individuals take the next steps toward treatment.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to contribute to your team.

Sincerely,

Stephanie Nuñez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With over nine years of experience in behavioral health services, including more than six years with Metrocare, I have developed a strong foundation in client engagement, psychosocial rehabilitation, care coordination, and supporting individuals with diverse mental health needs. I am confident that my experience, communication skills, and commitment to helping individuals access appropriate care would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your team.

Throughout my career, I have worked with children, adolescents, and adults, providing skills training and psychosocial rehabilitation services to support emotional well-being, daily functioning, and progress toward individualized treatment goals. My experience has strengthened my ability to build rapport, communicate with individuals and families, recognize barriers to care, and connect clients with appropriate resources and services. I understand the importance of approaching individuals and families with empathy, professionalism, and sensitivity, particularly when they are navigating mental health challenges or seeking support during difficult circumstances.

I recognize that the admissions process is often a critical first step in a family’s treatment journey. I would bring a compassionate, organized, and client-centered approach to helping families navigate that process, gathering relevant information, coordinating communication, and supporting timely access to appropriate treatment services. My behavioral health background has also equipped me to communicate effectively with multidisciplinary teams, maintain professional documentation, manage competing priorities, and approach sensitive situations with discretion and respect.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to apply my clinical experience in a role focused on connecting adolescents and families with the support and treatment they need. I value collaboration, accountability, and clear communication, and I am committed to helping create a positive and supportive experience from the initial point of contact through the admissions process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, client-centered approach, and dedication to improving access to care align with the needs of your organization. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your team.

Sincerely,
Sandra M. Scruggs

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. Throughout my career in case management, higher education, crisis response, and community outreach, I have dedicated myself to helping individuals and families navigate difficult circumstances and access the support they need. Your commitment to providing adolescents with a safe, compassionate, and supportive environment strongly resonates with both my professional experience and personal values.

As a Case Manager with the Care & Assistance Team at Texas A&M University–Corpus Christi, I supported students experiencing mental health concerns, housing instability, financial hardship, family difficulties, and other challenges affecting their well-being. I conducted needs assessments, developed individualized action plans, coordinated referrals, and collaborated with campus and community partners to connect students with appropriate services. This experience strengthened my ability to recognize when individuals need additional support, respond with empathy, and provide consistent follow-up while respecting confidentiality and professional boundaries.

My experience as a Pretrial Officer for Bexar County further developed my ability to manage complex caseloads, assess individual circumstances, maintain accurate documentation, and connect individuals with community resources. Previously, as a police dispatcher and 911 operator, I learned to remain calm under pressure, communicate clearly during emergencies, and respond to sensitive situations with sound judgment. These experiences prepared me to work effectively with individuals experiencing distress while maintaining professionalism and compassion.

My commitment to helping vulnerable populations also extends into my community involvement. Through Ferro Family Ministries, our family's nonprofit organization, I have collaborated with churches and community volunteers across Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Mexico to support underserved youth and families. Our outreach efforts have included helping individuals access basic necessities, coordinating charitable assistance, and organizing fundraising initiatives for families facing significant hardships. These experiences reinforced my belief that meaningful support begins with listening, understanding individual needs, and treating every person with dignity and respect.

I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy's focus on supporting teenagers and their families through challenging periods in their lives. I understand the importance of building trust, communicating without judgment, and working collaboratively with professionals and families to promote stability and positive outcomes. While my background is not in clinical counseling, I bring extensive experience in client support, crisis communication, resource coordination, and compassionate service.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my skills and dedication to Adolescent Wellness Academy's mission. 
Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my experience can support your team and the adolescents and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Michael A. Ferro

My name is Samantha Gibbs and I am looking for an Intake/Admissions Coordinator position where I can offer emotional-social support for individuals and families with mental health diagnoses while contributing to a welcoming and helpful environment. I have developed counseling and crisis counseling skills I would love to apply to this job. I am interested in making a career pivot into admissions behavioral health services as I am passionate about stabilizing clients/patients. I am familiar with case management in terms of effectively communicating support with clients, using behavioral health knowledge and experience, and taking care of administrative tasks. I have extensive experience, as well as education, in crisis counseling and behavioral health. My enthusiasm for working with people and providing service is largely found in my experiences helping others through crisis and I believe I would excel in the work environment described. My primary population worked with has been children, adolescents, and families, which I also focus on in my undergraduate studies.
I am enthusiastic about working with Adolescent Wellness Academy and I hope to bring my passion and care for people’s mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy by offering friendliness and behavioral health support to clients. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Samantha Gibbs

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With my professional background in substance use treatment and behavioral health, combined with my experience using Kipu and providing services through telehealth, I believe I would bring a valuable combination of clinical knowledge, technical proficiency, and compassion to your admissions team.

Throughout my career as a substance use disorder therapist and behavioral health professional, I have worked extensively with individuals experiencing addiction, co-occurring mental health conditions, trauma, and other complex challenges. My experience spans residential treatment, Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP), and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP). This familiarity with multiple levels of care allows me to explain treatment options confidently, recognize individual needs, and help prospective clients and their families navigate what can often be an overwhelming process.

I also have hands-on experience with Kipu electronic medical records, clinical documentation, treatment coordination, and telehealth services. I understand the importance of accurate recordkeeping, confidentiality, HIPAA compliance, and timely communication in ensuring continuity of care. My clinical background has also strengthened my ability to work independently, prioritize responsibilities, and collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams.

Perhaps my greatest strength is my ability to connect with people, particularly during vulnerable or emotionally difficult moments. I understand that individuals reaching out for treatment may be frightened, hesitant, or unsure where to begin. I believe the first interaction with a treatment provider should communicate compassion, reassurance, and hope while offering clear, practical guidance toward the next step.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to use my clinical experience in a different but equally meaningful capacity. I recognize that the admissions process is often the beginning of someone's recovery journey, and I would find tremendous purpose in helping individuals and families access the care they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, familiarity with Kipu, and commitment to compassionate, client-centered care could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Chloé

Eau Claire, WI
October 21, 2026
Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy & Principles Recovery Center
Subject: Application for Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position for Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Your job description talks about being the first voice someone hears on one of the hardest days of their lives, and that really stuck with me. While I don't have formal hospital admissions or boarding department experience, I have spent years working right on the front lines of care. I have worked in group homes with adults dealing with mental health and addiction, in daycares, and as an activities coordinator in senior care. I know exactly how to talk to people going through a crisis, and I know how to keep things calm, supportive, and completely confidential.
In my care background, I am very used to being the main person families and providers talk to when they need help. I am completely comfortable answering phone calls, listening closely to what a family is going through, and explaining how a program works in plain, simple language so they feel at ease. I am also incredibly structured when it comes to the paperwork side of things. I know how critical it is to follow up consistently so that no one gets left behind, and I pride myself on staying organized so that every single detail is tracked properly.
I am fully prepared to handle this role in a remote environment. I am highly self-motivated, stick to a disciplined routine, and manage my daily tasks independently without needing someone to watch over my shoulder. I am used to working with data tracking systems and software platforms, and I take details and HIPAA compliance very seriously. Plus, my background in early childhood education gives me an intuitive understanding of the developmental struggles that the teenagers and families reaching out to AWA are facing.
I would love the opportunity to talk with you about how my real-world care experience, confident phone presence, and dedication to behavioral health can help support your admissions team. Thank you so much for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Emilita

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

When a family or individual reaches out during one of the most vulnerable moments of their life, the very first voice they hear can shape their entire path toward healing. As a dedicated mental health advocate with extensive experience managing high-stakes crisis situations, active listening, and complex multi-platform coordination, I am thrilled to submit my application for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) and Principles Recovery Center (PRC).

My professional background is centered on de-escalating high-stress situations, building immediate trust, and guiding individuals toward safe, actionable next steps. In my current work handling real-time safety alerts and through my formal training as a 988 Crisis Hotline volunteer counselor, I am deeply accustomed to meeting people in moments of distress with warmth, composure, and zero judgment. Whether explaining levels of care, walking a worried parent through the intake process, or addressing common hesitations surrounding PHP and IOP treatment, I focus on creating a safe, human connection while ensuring seamless operational execution.

Mental health advocacy is not just my career focus; it is my life’s work. To further deepen my clinical foundation and long-term impact in behavioral health, I am actively enrolling in a counseling degree program next year. This academic commitment, paired with my daily crisis training and hands-on remote experience, allows me to speak about behavioral health and substance use care with authority, clarity, and deep personal empathy.

In addition to my human-centered approach, I thrive in fast-paced, fully remote environments where self-management and technological agility are essential. I am highly proficient in managing high-volume candidate and client pipelines using CRM systems, double-checking documentation for strict compliance, and tracking follow-ups so that no caller falls through the cracks.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my blend of crisis intervention skills, remote workflow precision, and passion for adolescent and adult recovery can support AWA and PRC’s growth. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Warmly,

Lanrella Barber
